title: Your first steps into AI
description: A practical beginner roadmap for learning AI without a technical background or expensive course.

sections.title: Start with a task you understand
sections.body: You do not need to learn every model, acronym, or app. Choose a familiar task, such as summarizing a public article or drafting a personal study plan. Familiarity lets you notice errors. Use invented or public information while you learn, and check that your chosen tool is approved before using it for work.
bullets: Start with one tool and one small task.
Keep the original information beside the answer.

sections.title: Learn through a simple practice loop
sections.body: Give the tool a clear instruction, inspect the response, and change one thing in the instruction. Notice what improved and what did not. Keep a small record of the task, prompt, result, and correction. Learning this loop builds a transferable skill even when specific products change.
bullets: Compare a vague prompt with a specific prompt.
Ask for an explanation of an unfamiliar term, then explain it in your own words.

sections.title: Build a manageable learning routine
sections.body: Spend your first few sessions understanding limitations, privacy, and prompting. Next, complete one realistic project. Finally, explain your process to someone else. Progress means you can select a suitable task, recognize a weak result, and improve it. Finishing a course is useful, but it is not the only evidence that you can work well with AI.
bullets: Practice for a short, repeatable period.
Measure the quality of the work, not the number of tools you tried.

example.title: A first-week plan
example.text: Day 1: understand the basics. Day 2: practice a clear prompt. Day 3: verify an answer. Day 4: review privacy. Day 5: complete a small task and record what you learned. Repeat anything that still feels unclear.

exercise: Choose one public article. Ask for a five-point summary, verify every point, and rewrite the weakest point yourself.

faq.question: Can I learn AI without coding?
faq.answer: Yes. Using AI responsibly, writing clear prompts, checking outputs, and improving workflows do not require programming. Building AI software may require additional technical skills.

faq.question: How long does it take to learn AI?
faq.answer: You can practice basic tasks in a few sessions. Reliable use in a profession takes continuing practice, feedback, and relevant subject knowledge.

sources.name: European Commission: AI literacy questions and answers
